title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
Profaned Capital -  Dark Souls III - location - lore 
 lore : The Profaned Capital was ruled over by Yhorm the Giant, descendant of an ancient conqueror, who was nevertheless asked by the previously subjugated people to lead them. A sorcery school was established there, one of two leading schools claiming to be heir to the legacy of Big Hat Logan. The court sorcerers from the Profaned Capital also served as priests, as golden stitching of their robes suggest. Although they were undeniably intelligent and adept in their craft, it is possible that they did not follow Big Hat Logan as much as they claimed to. Despite the Citizens of the Profaned Capital called Yhorm "King", their hearts were not their voice, meaning they merely used him and didn't trust him.

title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
Profaned Capital -  Dark Souls III - location - theories 
 theories : It's possible that the Profaned Capital was part of the kindgom of Carthus, and that the city declared independence from said kingdom.
** Yhorm is said to be the descendant of an ancient conqueror, and the only conqueror mentioned in the game is Wolnir.
** Both countries apply the use of pyromancies.
** Wolnir's use of the abyss and his following discovery of Dark Pyromancies may have prompt the Court Sorcerers to study the dark and the abyss, leading to the creation of the Profamed Flame.
It's possible that the one dear to Yhorm was his wife, and that Leonhard is their son. Leonhard is said to be a member of royalty, that was taught sorcery, and that was burned in his young age, and the Profaned Capital is a country of sorcerers burned by the profaned flame.

title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
Profaned Capital -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : The Profaned Capital is a highly decimated ruin that has somehow sunken into a great chasm, the only natural light pouring from a crack in the cavernous walls. Very little of what was once a proud civilization remains, making this area quite small. The state of the Capital is in such disarray that the only things remaining are a few bridges and tunnels, a vestige of a great tower, a church sunken in a swamp, and the throne room of Yhorm the Giant. The rest of what was once a prosperous realm has long since corroded away. An overlook of the Capital is viewable from Irithyll Dungeon.

One of two bonfires is within the central tower, its interior hollowed out, but its heights traversable thanks to numerous ladders up and down its interior and exterior. The source of the ladders is no mystery, as the corpse of Laddersmith Gilligan can be seen splayed out right by the bonfire, where the player can learn a gesture.

title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
Yhorm defended the kingdom from many threats, serving as the kingdom's heavy blade and solid shield, and at some point, Yhorm acquired two Storm Rulers, probably from the enemies he defeated. He gave one such sword to his subjects in an efford to win their trust.

As a result of a curse which bound a group of women which were four relatives of a priest (a court sorcerer), the everlasting Profaned Flame was triggered. Those involved in the curse went on living carelessly, although the curse turned the women into malformed creatures.. The sorcerers created Gargoyles that wield either spears, or hammers imbued with the Profaned Flame.

After Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder in order to stop the Profaned Flame, the city was burned down by a fire said to be coming from the sky, which burned only humans.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Yhorm the Giant -  Dark Souls III - boss - location 
 location : Found at the end of the Profaned Capital, in a large throne room located between two treasury rooms guarded by Jailer Handmaids, Mimics, and Gargoyles.

title: Profaned Capital
snippet:
After Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder in order to stop the Profaned Flame, the city was burned down by a fire said to be coming from the sky, which burned only humans.

The only survivors of the Capital are the Handmaids, the court sorcerer Eamon, and the four malformed women. The Handmaids who served in the Capital reportedly took pleasure in hurting others.

Sometime after the Profaned Flame destroyed the Capital, Pontiff Sulyvahn discovered the Profaned Flame and the Capital, "a burning ambition took root within him". He would later infuse the Profaned Flame within his own greatsword, and would perhaps introduce the Profaned Flame to the Fire Witches. They would learn to use its power and summon firestorms with their halberds., and would eventually take Irithyll for themselves.

Sulyvahn would later build a dungeon, and hired some handmaids to guard the prison, which preserves part of the profaned flame in a icy skull.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Yhorm the Giant -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the "great conqueror" from whom Yhorm descends is High Lord Wolnir, as the only character in the lore of Dark Souls III addressed as a great conqueror. In addition, Yhorm's immense size could be explained by his descent from Wolnir, also a gigantic humanoid. Again, the Catacombs of Carthus and the Profaned Capital, despite the convergence of the lands towards Lothric, are both underground and close together, implying that Wolnir had also conquered the Profaned Capital and that when Wolnir was overwhelmed by the Abyss, only his son remained as potential heir who could reign over the conquered city.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet: It is possible to theorize that the event in which the Profaned Flame went out of control, destroying the Profaned Capital, was the result of a Court Sorcerers ritual gone awry. In fact, these sorcerers did not care about their creations even when they were as dangerous as the dark flame, continuing to live as if nothing had happened, driven by an unethical and unruly pursuit of knowledge. In addition, the only survivors of the destruction of the city are a noble court sorcerer and the handmaids, possibly in the noble's service, implying that someone had somehow managed to avoid being devoured by the flame. Furthermore, the detail of the Profaned Flame "falling" from the sky and devouring only human beings implies an unnatural event in which the flame was not in its previous controlled conditions but was activated toward human targets.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - profaned_capital 
 profaned_capital : Descending through the dungeon of Irithyll brings the Ashen One to the Profaned Capital, home of the reclusive Yhorm the Giant, one of the missing lords. Fighting their way past the gargoyles and priestesses that guard the way to the giant, the Ashen One finds him atop his throne. The enormously strong and durable Yhorm initially seems insurmountable, but the Ashen One finds the magic blade Storm Ruler, a sword with the ability to fell giants, beside his throne. Using the power of the blade, the Ashen One is able to bring Yhorm to his knees and kill him, collecting his ashes.

title: Catarina
snippet: At a certain point Catarina came into contact, on a conflict or diplomatic level, with the Profaned Capital, and Yhorm the Giant, the ruler of the city became a great friend of the knight Siegward. Before facing his fate as a Lord of Cinder and linking the First Flame, Yhorm made Siegward promise to kill him if he were ever exhumed from his grave, gifting him a weapon capable of killing him easily.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet: It is possible to theorize that Yhorm refused to serve as fuel for the First Flame a second time due to the fact that, once awakened from his grave, he realized that his sacrifice had been futile. The sorcerers of the Profaned Capital had continued to experiment on the Profaned Flame he had tried to quell with his sacrifice and as a result the entire city was destroyed, making his life of service meaningless even after the end. The moment he rises from the grave, he can be seen already howling in despair. In addition, he may also have simply understood the state of the world, now corrupted beyond any possibility of traditional salvation through the linking of the Fire, and simply decided to await death in the ruins of his city.

title: Timeline
snippet:
Yhorm, as one of the previous Lords of Cinder, is exhumed from his graves to use the embers of the Flame still within him as fuel for it
Yhorm refuses to contribute to the linking of the Flame once again and instead returns to the Profaned Capital
Yhorm remains on his throne inside the city's ruins to prevent further disastrous uses of the Profaned Flame

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Yhorm the Giant -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Yhorm, normally spelled Jorm, is an Old Norse word meaning "huge". It appears in the name of the Norse world-serpent *Jormungandr*, literally "huge monster". The spelling Yhorm may help with pronunciation, as the letter J is usually pronounced in Old Norse as a Y.
His appearance seems unique to giants. For one he is the only living giant with facial features, consisting of two bright red eyes and an angular jawline. His proportions are very similar to human proportions, unlike most giants in the games, and he appears to be taller than the giants of Anor Londo.
A player version of Yhorm's armor set exists in the game files, but it is not available to the player under normal circumstances.
Despite being one of the easiest bosses to beat, Yhorm has the highest HP of any boss in *Dark Souls III* (including Darkeater Midir, Sister Friede, and The Demon Prince).

When there were those who doubted him, he gave them a giant-slaying sword, to show his trustworthiness. He risked everything for his people in the frontlines, fighting valiantly as a one-man vanguard. It is stated that he lost someone dear to him and, as a result, he forsook his greatshield. Afterwards, he notched his machete to allow for two hand use, giving him an even more ferocious fighting style. At some point, "lonely" Yhorm befriended Siegward of Catarina, who became a dear friend of his.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: While the Giants invasion was largely stopped, their souls remained powerful. King Vendrick's elder brother, Lord Aldia, kept Giants in his manor and performed experiments on them in an attempt to recreate a dragon. The outcome of Lord Aldia's experiments is unknown, but oddly when the Ancient Dragon roosting at the summit of Aldia's realm was slain, the soul of a Giant was found in its remains. Legend holds that the Giants' resentment of King Vendrick was possibly emboldened in death. This was proven true when the Bearer of the Curse fought the hollowed remains of Vendrick. With the souls of several Giants in the Bearer's possession, Vendrick was significantly weakened and subsequently defeated.

title: Captain Drummond
snippet: What happened to Drummond afterwards is never stated, but his armor, sword and shield can be found in the ruins of the fort, now enveloped by the surrounding forest, around the wall where the Giant Lord was felled in the past. It is therefore likely that he perished shortly after the victory on the Giants, becoming the last of his family line. The absence of his helm is also meaningful, as he gifted it to the Bearer of the Curse in the past for helping his remaining army in their hour of need.

title: Giants (Lore)
snippet: After the end of the great war, Lord Gwyn and his clan gained dominion over the world and began their Age of Fire, with the giants continuing to coexist with their civilization in a subordinate but close position. A number of giants became Sentinels guarding the walls and streets of Anor Londo, the city of the gods, employing giant halberds made of brass and retaining the power of lightning, giant shields of white iron, and heavy armor of finely decorated golden brass. An even more powerful group of giants defended the royal cathedral in the center of the city and were capable of performing restorative and offensive miracles.

 lead : is a boss in *Dark Souls III* and one of the five Lords of Cinder encountered by the Ashen One in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Seeking vengeance for the subjugation of his kingdom, the king of the Giants amassed an army in a vengeful counter-invasion of Drangleic. He also sought to reclaim the invaluable "prize" stolen from him. Unwilling to forgive the actions of Vendrick, the Giants crossed the sea and landed on the northern shores of Drangleic. They set siege to Drangleic Castle and relentlessly attacked various settlements, forts and keeps across the land for several generations.

title: Giant (Dark Souls II)
snippet: Battles waged endlessly between Vendrick's forces and the Giants, and much of Drangleic's citizens fled the kingdom to escape the conflict. Ultimately, the Giants were defeated by an unnamed hero. In the aftermath, much of Drangleic had been reduced to rubble, and visitors to the kingdom were rare. Many Giants were killed in the conflict, and their corpses eventually grew into large trees that sprawled across the once prosperous kingdom. The last known Giant to have survived the conflict was terribly wounded and kept prisoner in a cavern beneath the Forest of Fallen Giants. It was later discovered another two Giants survived the war, but remained hidden in a cavern in Black Gulch.

title: Yhorm's Greatshield
snippet:
Yhorm's Greatshield -  Dark Souls III - weapon - characteristics 
 characteristics : Yhorm's Greatshield is on the heavier end of greatshields, being in the same weight class as titans like the Moaning Shield and Stone Greatshield.

To back up its heavy weight, Yhorm's Greatshield provides strong all-round defenses and very high stability, allowing it to shrug off most attacks with minimal stamina damage and negligible chip elemental damage. What makes it unique among greatshields, however, is that it increases the player's Poise by 15% while wielded, a trait shared only by the Lothric Knight Long Spear. As such, it pairs well with large Hyper Armor weapons, allowing the wielder to more easily win trades against foes foolish enough to engage.

title: Gargoyle
snippet:
Gargoyle -  Dark Souls III - enemy - profaned_capital 
 profaned_capital : Gargoyles encountered in the Profaned Capital are often positioned on bridges or rooftops, so the player should be mindful of their surroundings when engaging them in combat. They will disguise themselves as regular statues and will spring to life when in close proximity, although striking them with a ranged weapon will trigger them early. Their attacks inflict Fire damage and they can block attacks with their wings. If struck during this, they will retaliate with a shunt that can send the player flying.

Gargoyles will often take flight and attempt to strike the player from above before crashing down on top of them. By running underneath when they jump, it is possible to sprint past them.

If he survives the encounter, he will give the player one final Siegbräu. Upon reloading the arena, his armor set, shield and Storm Ruler can be found within the arena. If the player has already defeated Yhorm before freeing Siegward from the cell in the Profaned Capital, the Storm Ruler will appear as a drop in the boss area, but the player will not receive his armor set nor shield or Siegbräu.

title: Jailer's Key Ring
snippet:
Jailer's Key Ring -  Dark Souls III - item - availability 
 availability : Found in the upper levels of the Giant Slave's cell in the Irithyll Dungeon. To reach it, the player must head through the toxic swamp of the Profaned Capital, up the chapel, and through a passage with a hole on the wall overlooking the giant and guarded by two invisible Jailers. The key lies at the end of the hallway.

title: Azal, Sage of Forossa
snippet:
Azal, Sage of Forossa -  Dark Souls II - character - lore 
 lore : Azal was an accomplished sage of Forossa, one of the Northwarders who earn their title after surviving a journey of great hardship. He was exceptionally skilled as he imbued his staff with magic, granting it unique powers. This made the tool unwieldy for the inexperienced, which proved the sage's magical prowess.

What became of him is unknown, but his staff can be retrieved on a corpse in Eleum Loyce, a kingdom ruled by a Forossan champion. It's possible, then, that Azal died in the frozen city, perhaps while investigating what had happened to it.

title: Gargoyle
snippet:

The first gargoyle attacks as the player crosses the bridge that connects the Irithyll Dungeon with the Profaned Capital.

A third will also attack midway through a bridge, this time on the one that leads toward Yhorm's arena and that is being bombarded by fireballs from afar.
Two more will attempt to ambush the player along groups of Jailer Handmaids in the treasury, one on each wing of the building.

title: Cursebite Ring (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Cursebite Ring (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - ring - availability 
 availability : Found in the Profaned Capital.

From the Profaned Capital bonfire, climb down the ladder and exit through a hole in the wall. The path eventually leads to a toxic swamp and the ruins of a chapel. Drop into the swamp and head inside a cavern inhabited by several Sewer Centipedes on the opposite side of the chapel. The ring can be found on a corpse within such cavern.

title: Pontiff Sulyvahn
snippet: One day, when Sulyvahn was still young, he unearthed the Profaned Capital underneath the outskirts of Irithyll; he also discovered in the ruins of the city the Profaned Flame. It was a "cold" flame, found preserved in icy remains; it was an unfading, everlasting flame, and one that held within it the Dark of humanity. Having obtained the sinful flame, an unquenchable ambition took root in Sulyvahn's heart, as the young man understood its potential as an element of immense political and religious power: The First Flame would eventually fade, while his Profaned Flame was everlasting.

title: Archive Tower Giant Cell Key

Archive Tower Giant Cell Key -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Key to the giant cell below the Duke's Archives Tower. The giant cell once imprisoned countless maidens, but is now empty, save for a few key persons. They struggle to uphold their sanity, as the horde of "mistakes" writhe at a fearfully close proximity.

title: Archive Tower Giant Door Key
snippet:
Archive Tower Giant Door Key -  Dark Souls - item - description 
 description : Key to the giant door leading out from the uppermost floor of Archive Tower, which now serves as a prison.

The key's design resembles not the key of a prison; indeed, the tower was once no prison at all, but a trove of precious tomes.
